subject: humanities
passage: When foods traveled from one part of the world to another, their names often traveled with them. ______ the English word "tomato" comes from tomatl, a word in Nahuatl, the language of the Aztecs. The Aztecs grew tomatoes in Mexico long before Spanish traders brought the plant to Europe in the 1500s.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The first sentence makes a general claim: food names often moved along with the foods. The next sentence gives one case of this, the word "tomato," which came to English from Nahuatl. A transition that introduces an example is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "For example" introduces "tomato" as one case of a food name traveling with the food.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean the tomato's name replaced the general pattern, but it fits the pattern.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The general pattern did not cause this word to come from Nahuatl; the word is one instance of the pattern.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The history of "tomato" supports the general claim instead of contrasting with it.
